An organic compound contains C, H and S. The minimum molecular weight of the compound containing 8% sulphur is :

(atomic weight of S = 32 amu)

400 g mol<sup><mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.186ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.76ex" height="1.505ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -583 778 665" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mo"><use data-c="2212" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-2212"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>1</sup>

en.explanation:
We know that 8% sulphur means 8 g of sulphur present in 100 g of an organic compound.

Thus, 32 g of sulphur present in = 400 g of organic compound.

Therefore, minimum molecular weight of the compound is 400 g mol1.

C(s) + O2(g) CO(s)

options.content: At T > 1200 K, carbon will reduce MO(s) to M(s).

At T < 1200 K, the reaction

MO(s) + C(s) M(s) + CO(g) is spontaneous.
At T < 1200 K, oxidation of carbon is unfavourable
Oxidation of carbon is favourable at all temperatures.

en.explanation: Carbon is a good reducing agent for oxides. The reason why carbon reduces metal oxide spontaneously at T < 1200 K is that line for CO has a negative slope.
